We introduce an innovative technique that synergistically combines inter-domain loss and CycleGAN to facilitate semi-supervised end-to-end automatic speech recognition. Inter-domain loss aims to derive a common speech-text representation through a shared neural network, whereas CycleGAN leverages cycle-consistency and identity mapping to preserve input characteristics after cross-domain conversion. As both approaches can train end-to-end models with unpaired data, we leverage their strengths to improve the speech-text mapping and shared representation, ultimately enhancing speech recognition performance. Our experimental findings on the WSJ, Voxforge, and LibriSpeech datasets reveal significant reductions in character error rate (approximately 8-8.5%), surpassing the baseline performance and exhibiting noticeable improvements on LibriSpeech test_clean.

This study introduces a innovative method of active prediction for robots to use when navigating through complex environments. The approach relies on a sophisticated camera system called an RGBD camera that enables the robot to build a 3D model of its surroundings in real time. By employing a specially designed deep neural network model, the robot can accurately calculate where to go based on the resulting 3D data. However, this prediction requires constant updating as the robot moves, and incorporating new data while minimizing disruption to its navigation is crucial. To address this challenge, the robot can engage in active prediction, focusing on 3D data streams to pinpoint two specific objects it is interested in and then adjust its camera settings to ensure seamless 3D model updating and continued navigation.

To explain the Soret effect in polymers, a model has been proposed by Kanaya, which demonstrates that the separation of heat and molecules along the temperature gradient is accelerated when flexible molecules adopt various orientations. This concept was tested by simulating a polymer molecule consisting of a rigid backbone and freely rotating arms in an arbitrary temperature profile. The results showed that the arms of the molecule tend to gather on the cooler side. This phenomenon's contribution can be quantified by the diffusion coefficient for structural changes in the molecule. The magnitude of this coefficient correlates with the degree to which the arms orient themselves in response to the temperature difference. This behavior was also observed in a model polymer based on phenyl groups, which undergo rotational freedom.

The evaluation of written skills through automated essay assessment has gained significant interest in recent years, but its widespread adoption is limited by the need for large, high-quality datasets. When such resources are scarce, the solution lies in developing advanced machine learning techniques that can efficiently utilize the data available. This work proposes two novel approaches to automated essay assessment. The first approach involves utilizing a pre-trained BERT model, which has been fine-tuned on a subset of essays, to assign grades based on their textual content. Furthermore, this method's scalability and generalizability are enhanced by leveraging a technique that allows for the assessment of multiple grades and domains. Notably, our analysis demonstrates that a simplified, yet efficient version of the transformer model (known as AlBERT) yields the most accurate evaluations across different essay domains and grades.

One of the most critical components of autonomous vehicle systems is the pedestrian detection module, which necessitates extremely high accuracy to ensure passenger safety, despite the limited availability of annotation data, particularly in challenging domain-adaptation scenarios. Suppressed false positives might eventually contribute to system improvement. Therefore, we introduce an innovative technique, called Box Re-Ranking, which employs a low-cost network to assess the confidence of detection boxes, focusing on previously suppressed ones. This method can be efficiently trained in an entirely unsupervised manner within a self-tuning framework. Moreover, to accelerate the process, we introduce a Distillation-by-Similarity approach to achieve rapid convergence. Experimental results show that our solution yields improved performance in both conventional and domain-adaptability settings, such as adaptive pedestrian detection across day-night scenarios.

This study presents an innovative method for enhancing low-quality music recordings made on portable devices by leveraging neural-based image processing and audio conversion techniques. The objective of the former is to cleanse the visual manifestations of noise and distortions, while the latter aims to generate high-fidelity audio suitable for listening or archival purposes. By combining these techniques with a well-established method for improving recorded audio quality, we achieve substantial quality gains through an end-to-end process. Notably, our results demonstrate that the simplest form of our image processing model produces comparable outputs to a cutting-edge music restoration model. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive examination of the complexities involved in developing successful music restoration models.

Our primary objective is to comprehensively investigate the impact of a ball's point of release on viewers' perception of a throwing motion. Our research spans data collection, thorough analysis of a throwing motion rendered as linear interpolation, and the development of FauxThrow, a realistic rendering system for arbitrary release points that combines physics-based information with visually compelling techniques like texture mapping and color gradiation. By conducting a thorough investigation of varying release points and incorporating the opinions of both professional coaches and casual observers, we aim to offer actionable insights for the creation of more authentic throwing effects in visual media. Ultimately, our research findings demonstrate the clear distinction made by humans between a throwing motion with a point of release and one without, and highlight the significant role of visual cues like ball texture and color in the recognition of a throwing motion.

To incorporate syntax-aware decoding into Neural Machine Translation systems, a novel cascaded decoding framework is presented, combining the advantages of analysis and generation in a single, optimized model. This innovative approach, built on existing state-of-the-art models, enhances its word generation capabilities by considering syntax-derived information. The new framework is evaluated on the I18n dataset, yielding notable improvements in translation quality. Furthermore, a concurrent study investigates the impact of this new decoding strategy on parsing tasks, demonstrating its potential to reduce decoding list size and accelerate search speed. The proposed model is expected to contribute significantly to the fields of Machine Translation and Syntax-Parsing, offering a unique opportunity to explore the interplay between these tasks within the context of the Transformer architecture.

Accurate calculations of binding energies are crucial for understanding the complex chemical reactions and decompositions in interstellar environments and extraterrestrial ices. Though this task can be computationally demanding for vast datasets of molecules, modern advancements in theoretical and laboratory methods make it necessary to assess the validity of the resulting binding energy values. A new tool, the Binding Energy Assessment Platform, provides a framework for comparing experimental and theoretical binding energies to determine accurate values. Based on a previous study (Berlow et al., 2020), the BEAP platform offers a database with pre-calculated binding energy distributions for over 170 ice molecules. This database includes a wide range of compounds with diverse molecular structures, which can serve as a standard reference for future simulations and experiments, promoting collaboration and streamlining the evaluation of binding energy values. By promoting collaboration and streamlining the evaluation of binding energy values, the BEAP platform facilitates calculations that can accurately determine the binding energies for any given molecule within its specified range.

A multiplicative stochastic process is studied where each state's lower bound depends on previous states, leading to a phenomenon where extensive observation yields more certain outcomes. The studied SAR process, representing a sample-dependent model based on random variables, was found to have a general expression using log-linear functions. Criteria such as convergence in probability and almost sure uniqueness were established for the SAR process. The research also explores the potential applications of this process in generating random numbers and constructing stochastic algorithms for optimization.

In the field of quantum statistical mechanics, a new method is developed to accurately simulate thermodynamic properties of both simple and complex systems, without needing deep quantum circuits. This is achieved by analyzing the behavior of quantum states under specific types of operations called random Clifford circuits, which are relatively easy to implement and study. By increasing the depth of these circuits, the accuracy of their predictions can significantly increase. Ultimately, this approach can be seen as a form of 'quantum-informed' classical statistical mechanics, offering a useful resource for understanding the interplay between quantum systems and their thermodynamic properties.

The researchers who studied planar solutions of integrated Davey-Stewartson II equations discovered a significant growth in the reflection coefficient, $R(0,k)$, with increasing absolute value of $k$. This reflection coefficient determines wave reflection in a rotating, infinite water basin with a stationary surface, given a given topographic shape. In particular, they analyzed solutions of the integrated Davey-Stewartson II equations over functions $z(x,y)$, allowing for periodic changes in the variables. This led to a set of conditions under which $R(0,k)$ would behave differently at low and high values of $|k|$. This research reveals the effect of the bottom's irregularity on the corresponding Schrödinger equation, given a given rotation rate.

DeepRob, a novel text classification approach, enhances the Sibyl variant of query-based adversarial attacks by utilizing a deep learning model to improve the robustness of its predictions. This method operates by generating an alternative hypothesis for each sample in a training dataset using a classifier that is susceptible to adversarial attacks. Ultimately, DeepRob's prediction is based on a weighted average of the original and alternative hypotheses. Notably, deep learning models can be used in place of the initial black-box classifier, resulting in a more robust and accurate adversarial robustness assessment. This assessment is supported by experiments and analysis conducted on 13 datasets. Interestingly, it's discovered that deep learning models can sometimes produce rival hypotheses with similar or greater accuracy to the initial ones, highlighting a potential generalization issue for model agnostic assessments of adversarial robustness.

For a meta-learning algorithm to be practical, it must successfully handle
large-scale datasets. Unlike previous studies, this research focuses on
developing meta-learning concepts suitable for datasets of enormous scale.
Firstly, it introduces a new'meta-feature' type, using the initial (base)
coefficient set as input, instead of the entire training dataset as previous
studies have done. This allows base coefficient sets to be generated quickly,
and the algorithm remains efficient despite the dataset's size. Secondly, the
study introduces a new representation type - linear combinations of inputs -
which can easily be expanded to accommodate any dataset size, unlike other
representation types. This research provides theoretical justification for
linear combinations being an effective representation, as well as offering a
new interpretation of the meta-learning initial condition (WC1) through the
principle of Hermite Polynomials. The algorithms presented in this study are
not only theoretically justified but also show competitive results when
evaluated against other methods.

Building lightweight machine translation models has become a viable solution for limited-data scenarios but is hindered by the inconsistency between sparse models and sparse data, resulting in extremely sparse models that impair model adaptability. To address this issue, we investigated the potential of model compression techniques, specifically quantization and knowledge distillation, to create adaptable models without sacrificing performance. Our experiments, involving a variety of compression methods and configurations, demonstrate that distillation-based model compression yields more consistent improvements across a range of translation tasks, offering a promising solution for low-resource MT models.

A hypergraph is a collection of connected vertices through multiple edges.
The study of a hypergraph's properties begins with defining its Lagrangian
density as the ratio of its total edge weight to the number of edges present.
This paper focuses on a particular type of hypergraph known as "y-shapes", 
which have three edges of equal length and a specified orientation.
It is demonstrated that a specific y-shape hypergraph exists with a density 
close to $\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon$ for an infinitely small $\epsilon$, as well 
as its opposite, $\frac{1}{2}+\epsilon$. This finding establishes a new 
record for the most disimilar densities found in a single hypergraph type.

In image segmentation, the quantity of available labels directly correlates with the accuracy of the model for unseen data.  Typically, the boundary between supervised and semi-supervised learning is defined as the point where the number of labels exceeds the number of parameters.  When this threshold is exceeded, the role of the model shifts from adjusting its parameters based on the supervisory signals to utilizing those signals to improve its performance.  The following sections provide a brief overview of the key concepts in semi-supervised segmentation, an explanation of how image augmentation contributes to this area, and a demonstration of its application to a real-world scenario in a study on pneumonia detection in chest X-Ray images.

While Deep Learning based models can accurately recognize objects and describe images, their output often needs further refinement to match human expectations. This refinement is particularly important when using image description for applications that require a change in tone, such as to comply with social norms. Our proposed approach enables image description models to be regulated by a set of predefined prompts that control aspects such as the perspective, as seen in human-like descriptions, and the ability to include or exclude specific details. This control is achieved through iterative processing of the description with the aid of a pointer selector, allowing for a more tailored description. Our experiments, with both VGGImageCaption and CLIP, demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm in producing high-quality, prompt-dependent image descriptions. This improvement in image description capabilities also results in improved results when used in a text image diversity application. A user study showed that our image descriptions were judged to be as coherent and relevant as the original ones, but with the added benefit of being able to be controlled by the input prompt.

The concept of harm has become a prominent theme in both public discourse and
ethical policies, but the lack of a clear understanding of its scope has led to
both utilitarian overcautions and more recent attempts to refine its meaning.
Our analysis aims to build on existing philosophical theories by incorporating
empirical insights from psychology and sociology, and by distinguishing between
physical and psychological harm, we identify two main categories: infliction
(harm caused by an agent) and exclusion (Harm-causation, where an effect is
missed or diminished due to a specific reason). A hypothetical example - the
early treatment of Hansen's disease - is used to illustrate how different
theoretical frameworks can predict varying results in cases of exclusion. Our
work also explores the intersections and distinctions between these frameworks,
and how they might be integrated into a cohesive model of harm assessment.

This study showcases MMLSpark, an innovative open-source library that bridges the gap between Cognitive Toolkit and Apache Spark by introducing Java bindings and new components. The integration with OpenCV and the development of automated Pytorch converter in MMLSpark facilitates scalable deep learning operations on clusters, particularly with Pytorch models. The potential of MMLSpark is further demonstrated through empirical evidence of its performance, scalability, and usability compared to alternative libraries.

We are introducing an innovative zero-shot voice translation framework that can translate cross-lingual, with a particular focus on the genetic languages of Africa, given its severe lack of voice-based translation resources. By incorporating a source-agnostic encoding method, our system directly generates the target language's acoustic representation from the input audio signal, using a highly efficient and scalable architecture. To achieve this, we implement two crucial modifications: the target-encoder's source-agnostic encoding and a target-reconstructed loss for enhancing the system's output quality. Our experiments reveal that our proposed method produces translation outcomes that are on a par with their spoken counterparts, and our findings show that the zero-shot system is competitive with its fully-supervised counterpart on the ASRS speech translation task. Moreover, we make the essential software components of the model framework accessible via GitHub.

This work introduces a novel extension of the traditional heat conduction theory, grounded in the fundamental principles of Fourier's law and the entropic principle, with the addition of memory factors. The study also explores the behavior under these assumptions while considering the dynamic changes in boundary conditions over time, leading to the establishment of a nonlinear dynamic system of equations, along with a related stability issue related to the system's exponential convergence towards a stable equilibrium state.

Precise load forecasting is crucial for both energy management and the low voltage grid, especially in the context of smart energy systems. We investigated the challenge of predicting low voltage network load characteristics, particularly peak demand, from individual high resolution smart meter data. The introduction of multiple forecasting methods enables the calculation of a confidence interval for predicted load, which can enhance energy storage and grid operation decisions. The study examines the effectiveness of combining model based forecasting methods with historical average load values, particularly in the prediction of daily peak demands. Analysis of the results indicates that combining forecast types yields more accurate predictions than individual methods. The model output of kernel regression exhibits the lowest margin of error for peak demand forecasts. The inclusion of model based forecasting in energy data analytics can offer a valuable advantage in low voltage network management.

A comprehensive approach has been devised for integrating domain knowledge into machine learning algorithms in the context of textual data. A series of experiments has been conducted to evaluate the performance of the developed methods which utilize domain-specific rules as trained models to process textual data, thereby leveraging the benefits of both machine learning and expert knowledge. The effectiveness of the implemented rules has been assessed and those providing the greatest contributions have been selected for integration into the training process of a deep learning model. The resulting hybrid model has been tested on datasets containing labels derived from expert knowledge and from metadata. The performance metrics indicate that the hybrid model performs significantly better than corresponding models relying solely on machine learning or expert knowledge.

Creating a reliable model for precise COVID-19 detection on chest CT scans poses significant difficulties despite considerable advancements. The issue lies in the scarcity of detailed annotation, crucial for training accurate segmentation models. To overcome this problem, we present a new approach that combines segmentation and detection in a single model called SE-COD. The model utilizes a bi-level graph attention network to identify COVID-19 areas and subsequently refine the detection accuracy. The model can automatically convert detection results into segmentation outputs. Experiments on a large dataset indicate that SE-COD outperforms existing models and can handle previously unseen data. The project's code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/AI-SINCERE/SE-COD.

The growing field of spinal radiology attracts significant interest, driven by the need for accurate spine diagnosis, which traditionally relies on time-consuming manual vertebrae localization and identification techniques, however these methods fall short in everyday clinical settings. To address this challenge, this project offers an innovative automated solution that utilizes spine rectification and anatomical constraints to facilitate vertebrae localization and identification in CT scans, leading to notably improved precision and robustness, ultimately enabling reliable and accurate automated identification. Comprehensive assessments were conducted on a diverse dataset of CT images to evaluate the proposed approach, yielding outstanding results, demonstrating its potential to significantly streamline spinal CT reading and diagnosis.

Our study presents a dynamic electron scattering mechanism that operates within the ultrafast light-matter coupling regime, where strong, pulsed laser light interacts with matter. In this scenario, electron-nucleus pairs in a solid or liquid are perturbed by the pulsed radiation within an optical cavity. This interaction results in a temporary, resonant imbalance in the system's dynamics, caused by the correlation of photon vacuums that induces nuclear resonances. A theoretical model has been devised, and numerical simulations demonstrate that this imbalance can lead to the temporary storage of electrons in the conduction band, a effect that may be observed through measured changes in the energy distribution of electrons that have scattered off the nucleus.

In the field of control theory, traditional findings have posited that precise model knowledge is a prerequisite for implementing effective controllers. Nonetheless, research continuously uncovers that simplified models can impart invaluable insights, whereas overly detailed models can entangle important principles with superfluous details. This work innovates the field of legged locomotion by introducing a novel class of elastic actuators integrated into a simple bipedal model, resulting in an aggregation of relevant dynamics while omitting non-essential aspects. We demonstrate that a basic model encompassing only the pivotal factors can devise novel and sophisticated control methods, thereby reducing reliance on intricate models or expensive real-world experiments. Furthermore, this research showcases the applicability of this basic model to address intricate challenges in dynamics, mechanics, and control, underscoring the value of simplifying legislative frameworks in various scientific disciplines, especially when coupled with machine learning techniques, as exemplified here by a legged robot's gait controller.

A new approach has been developed for resolving the quantum separability problem by utilizing a linear variational intra-system invariant (LVIS) method, which exploits a distinct internal property of separable states. The novel combination of linear variational methods with group invariant theory enables more precise results for simpler systems and more reliable estimates for larger systems. The technique's performance is demonstrated through a range of non-negative eigenvalues of the Schmidt gap for various small and medium-scale systems across different quantum dimensions. Furthermore, monotonicity under partial transverse amplitude damping and ergodic control have also been investigated.

A theoretical framework is developed to explain the phenomenon of a ripplike mode in collisionless slab plasmas as observed in low-mode, long-wavelength scenarios. Our investigation focuses on the linear regime, yielding a dynamics description that distinguishes between two modes, one oscillatory and the other monotonic. Analysis of the monotonic mode indicates it maintains its character upon increasing the perturbation amplitude, in stark contrast to the oscillatory nature of the corresponding mode under such conditions. These findings align with results from a recent experiment described in reference \cite{dong2022observation}. Furthermore, this theoretical framework is versatile and can be applied to the study of various phenomena beyond just the ripping mode, encompassing other wave types in slabs, as well as geophysical scales.

The rise of e-commerce has transformed the fashion industry, with the efficient retrieval of similar garments through relevant images a long-sought goal. However, this objective has been hindered by the challenges of collecting sufficient labeled data, given the vast diversity of fashion items. To address this limitation, we have developed a novel approach to fashion-based retrieval, centred on manipulating fashion images at the feature level to enhance matching between queries and similar-looking items, thereby overcoming the constraints of traditional supervised methods. Notably, our semi-supervised solution only requires limited labeled data for good results. This innovative technique not only improves the similarity between images but also allows for the retrieval of more accurate fashion attributes, promoting innovative applications such as novel design creation and the discovery of similar garments for fashion designers.

The paper introduces an iterative procedure, referred to as the dual gradient method, specifically tailored for resolving functionally ill-posed problems within the realm of Banach spaces. By applying this approach, the minimization of a regularized objective function, formulated as a combination of the desired objective and a majorant, is achieved using subgradient optimization techniques. Utilizing decay rates of solution artifacts and the qualities of smoothness-inducing penalties enables the derivation of convergence rates for the dual gradient method, which surpass those obtainable through the standard first-order method. Consequently, the methodology yields fast, high-quality approximations of solution artifacts for operators having smoothness properties. Consequently, the methodology yields fast, high-quality approximations of solution artifacts for operators with smoothness properties.

Reconstructing the depth of a scene from light field images across different platforms has become a crucial task. This paper proposes a novel, end-to-end approach for estimating depth from light field images using a network called COAB. This dense, geometrically-constrained network is designed to handle the distortions present in every wavelength of each spherical input frame. By incorporating the cross-view distortions in each layer, COAB avoids separating these distortions into separate scales as found in other methods. This on-the-fly separation of distortions allows for the preservation of delicate scene features during training. Additionally, COAB's use of a distinct cost layer for calculating distances that incorporate scene occlusions prevents incorrect depth estimates for objects hidden from the viewer. By combining these processes with geometric relationships within the light field, COAB has achieved superior results on various metrics across multiple benchmark datasets when compared to other state-of-the-art approaches.

This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, first reducing the system and then employing double Wronskian solutions to yield a range of solutions for the resulting equations. Two novel solution families for the Fokas-Lenells equations are derived and illustrated through several examples. Furthermore, the paper also obtains new solutions for two reduced equations obtained from the Fokas-Lenells system via the Fokas-Lenells-Hone reduction.

The effective action for gravitational non-Riemannian metrics is formulated using double field theory, specifically within the framework of the polynomial Wilson action. This action has previously been shown to incorporate quantum corrections accurately. Calculations reveal that non-Riemannian terms emerge from the Wilson action at the same order as the Riemannian scalar curvature term, and can be generalized to various powers of curvature. Additionally, the anomalous Gravitational Magnetic Charge is derived, matching a prediction made by Aurbrecht et al. through anomaly analysis.

To optimize the performance of IEEE 802.11ac and above standard wireless connections in home networks, we propose an approach based on utilizing IEEE 802.11k/v technologies to monitor and manage the network. By leveraging these standards, we can gather information on wireless network configuration, locate access points and other devices, and make informed decisions about resource allocation. The main goal of this innovative method is to minimize the time it takes to associate with a new access point or extender after moving to a new location within the network. The proposed system involves the following key features: first, it identifies and manages noise levels by converting them into a numerical value and classifies them as either interference or dead spots; second, it uses signal strength and quality, along with physical separation, to locate devices and their coverage areas; third, it assigns new devices to the most suitable access point or extender based on their proximity and connection quality; and finally, it adjusts the configuration of each access point and extender to ensure that they are operating at their optimal capacity, and then applies an efficient path-adjustment algorithm to minimize the time it takes to associate with a new access point or extender. The method also allows it to adapt to changes in load and topology to maintain optimal performance. Evaluation of this approach through simulation reveals significant reductions in association time, with noise management achieving a 2.6-fold decrease and channel load management achieving a 1.5-fold decrease. By combining these methods, we can achieve even
